title: Column Subtractor
description: Put the greater number on top with the points in one line, trade across the point where a place is short, and undo a mistaken addition in two steps.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

stage.sizing: the frame is min(100vw, 177.78vh) wide and min(100vh, 56.25vw) tall (dvh where supported); the svg fills it. Nothing scrolls.

bands.header: 0 to 80. One line: the tool name, a measured dot, the phase concept; Hint, sound and restart as round controls far right.
bands.canvas: 92 to 640. One rounded card holding the key at its top right (Answer, Close, Enter, Next, or the Yes / No keys; no question bar), the working area (the whole card until Answer is tapped) and the answer drawer that slides in from the right; the summary page covers it at the end.
bands.footer: 652 to 900. The mascot at the far left on its ground line, the speech bubble beside it (y 656 to 892, the question and every line, printed), one small dot per phase at the right.

zones.layout: board, key only: no question bar, only its key at the right end of the top row (the question is on the bubble); the working area is the whole card (64, 108, 1472 x 520) until the child taps Answer, when the answer drawer (as tall as the working area, the key on its top row reading Close) slides in from the right
zones.controls: circles r 28 at cx 1388, 1460, 1532, cy 40: Hint (data-control again), sound, restart; 72-unit finger boxes
zones.dots: one small dot per phase at the footer's right (72-unit finger boxes, centred on the bubble), no text; in user AND AI mode each is a button (data-control phase-dot, data-phase k) that starts its phase

stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box on the stage. The score leaves on finished and onComplete and is shown once, as stars on the summary page.

writeup.why: Subtract decimals, from whole numbers too, with the points in one line and trading where a place is short, read the three wordings of subtraction, and undo a mistaken addition in two steps.
writeup.look: A column frame with one fixed point line, two cards lined up on it, trades drawn in vermilion above the columns, and a Wording card and an Undo panel on the later phases.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Column Subtractor' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x sixty-four, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: how many trades have been made, one for each block broken into ten. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x sixty-four, y 202. The frame spans x 110 to x 900 from y 230 to y 560, five columns 140 across headed Tens, Ones, Tenths, Hundredths and Thousandths, with the near-black point line at x 400. The two cards sit at y 300 and y 380, deep blue and labelled Given; the Top check outline lights amber around the upper card until it holds the greater number. A trade is drawn above its columns at y 250: one block of the left column breaks into ten small blocks of the short column, in vermilion, labelled Trade, and the top digits are rewritten there in small vermilion figures. The part taken away fades rose, labelled Taken away, and the difference is written green under a ruled line at y 500, labelled Difference. The Wording card sits at x 960, y 230, and the Undo panel at x 960, y 420, each 170 wide, stepping through its two steps one under the other. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is twelve number keys three across with a point key, for setting a decimal with up to three places or typing a difference into the answer slot. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the tools of this chapter share them. A decimal or fraction the question gives is deep blue, with the shaded parts that show it. The result the working reaches, a decimal, a fraction, a sum, a difference or what is left, is green, with its shaded parts. Ten of one place traded for one of the next, a carry in adding or a trade in taking away, is vermilion. A zero written after the point to line decimals up is violet, and so is the point written after a whole number before those zeros. The part taken away, used or poured out is rose. The digit, place or step being worked on now, and the first place where two decimals differ, are amber. A zero holding a place open inside a number is grey, and nothing else on the stage is ever grey. An unshaded part stays warm white inside its near-black outline, the decimal point is near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength rather than turning grey. Chrome never borrows one of them, and each of those readings survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label, Given, Answer, Carry, Trade, Added zero, Taken away, Left or Place holder, before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The card shows the last difference in the frame, every trade still in vermilion above its column.

writeup.delight: On the first phase, when a place is short and the child taps the column to its left, one block cracks open like a pod and ten small vermilion blocks tumble into the short column.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with the column frame drawn and its point line down the middle. On the first two phases the two cards wait in the tray with the Top check unlit, and on the second the upper card is a whole number with no point. On the third the Wording card shows its three wordings. On the fourth the Undo panel shows the mistaken answer. One thing moves, once: the first card, a wording or the Undo panel's first step gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line, and a finger on it is the whole way in.
writeup.freePlay: Any two decimals or whole numbers taken away with every trade shown, the Wording card and the Undo panel. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on trading across the point, taking from a whole number, three wordings, and undoing a mistake.
voiceLines: A column frame, waiting for the greater number on top.
Greater number on top. When a place is short, trade from the left.
Five has no tenths and no hundredths yet. What do you trade?
Three ways to say it. Which number starts on top each time?
First get back to the start. Then do the subtraction that was wanted.
New numbers. Greater on top, points in one line.
Free play. Take any decimal from a greater one.
Which number is on top? Is any place too short?
Every trade was shown, and every difference checked.

observations.observe: Every trade broke one block into exactly ten of the next place.

observations.why: its empty places after the point hold nothing to trade from until they are written.
observations.soWhat: a whole number gets its point and zeros before anything is taken from it.
observations.observe: A whole number needed its point and zeros before any trade could start.

observations.why: taking away undoes adding the same amount.
observations.soWhat: a mistaken addition is undone by taking the number away, then taking it away again.
observations.observe: Taking the added number away once brought back the starting number.

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, nothing resets, no colour means good or bad. The child's answer stays; the pad re-opens after the traceback.
tracebacks: Phase 1: The greater number goes on top with the points in one line and its zeros written in violet; each short place takes one block of its left neighbour, broken into ten (the old digit struck through in ink, the new one written above in vermilion); the difference is written green from the right, ending on the whole answer.

Phase 2: The whole number goes on top in the ones column and gets its point and zeros in violet; the trades run one place at a time, one one into ten tenths, then one tenth into ten hundredths (struck in ink, rewritten in vermilion); the difference is written green.

Phase 3: The Wording card lights the number every wording starts from; the frame puts it on top, writes the zeros, trades where a place is short and writes the difference green, the same difference for all three wordings.

Phase 4: The frame takes the added number away from the wrong result once and the start appears green; the start goes on top, the added number is taken away again, trading where short, and the right answer lands green.

voice.opening: A column frame, waiting for the greater number on top.
voice.onFreePlay: Free play: put the greater number on top, trade, take away, then try a new pair.
voice.onMiss: the item's own miss line, then the phase's two ladder rungs, shown at once UNDER the pinned instruction and kept until the child acts again
voice.onFinish: Every trade was shown, and every difference checked.
voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3, 4: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once. Present: rounded and clamped to one to 4; the tool starts at that phase and, as the NCERT tools do, walks on by itself after each phase's last question (its closing line, then 1.4 s), in user and AI mode alike, through phase 4 to the summary page (a tool with nextKey, runtime r48+: in user mode it waits for the child's blinking Next key instead, after every question and every phase, and the last phase's key opens the summary; AI mode, and a host that mounts one phase without navigableDots, walk on by themselves); finished once, from the summary page.
